H1-P4x: In the villages and families I've spent time around, a lot of the things we think we have to "re-invent" to form intentional communities are simply the way things are done. Land, childcare, housing, food, obligations, etc. etc. all get taken care of by the extended family and local memory, in addition to whatever formal systems there might be. Who needs a workshop called "Rebuilding Intergenerational Belonging" when some aunt has already given three people a task?
